Removes both provisions from the statutes.
sponsors: Rep. Humphrey, Rep. Saine, Sen. Hill

bills.title: Concealed Handguns On School Grounds
bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, bars concealed handgun permit holders from carrying on public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school grounds. Removes that limitation on permit holders. Leaves the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition untouched.

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruder At A Business
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against an unlawful intruder, under certain conditions, to more actors. Covers owners of a business. Also covers the managers and employees of the business.

bills.title: Legislative Approval For State Agency Fee Increase
bills.summary: Requires every state agency fee increase, beginning September 1, 2018, to take effect on July 1 of a year, with an exception for emergency increases. Bars an agency from raising a fee unless it submits a proposal with specified information to the joint budget committee by the preceding February 1, a majority of the committee approves it without alteration, and authorizing legislation granting the increase is enacted. Lets agencies adopt emergency fee increases outside that process. Requires an agency adopting an emergency increase to submit the proposal to the committee by the next February 1.

bills.title: Capitol Identification Card
bills.summary: Authorizes capitol security personnel, including the Colorado state patrol, to let holders of a state capitol ID card enter the capitol, state services, and legislative services buildings without a search of their person or property or weapons screening. Directs the secretary of the senate or the chief clerk of the house to issue the credential to any applicant who pays a fee and completes a fingerprint-based criminal history record check. Issues each credential for a 2-year period. Sets the initial fee at $100, with the amount set to cover the actual costs of administering the program.
sponsors: Sen. Cooke, Rep. Van Winkle, Rep. Williams

bills.title: Title 12 Relocation
bills.summary: Implements the initial recommendations of the recodification study of title 12, which covers professions and occupations. Relocates the Colorado Parental Notification Act to a new part of title 13 and the firearms dealer laws to a new part of title 18. Moves the gun show background check laws to title 18 as well, along with the Uniform Unsworn Declarations Act to title 13. Makes conforming amendments and repeals the provisions at their former locations.
sponsors: Sen. Cooke, Sen. Gardner, Rep. Herod, Rep. Foote

bills.title: Penalty For Burglary Of Firearms
bills.summary: Designates a third type of second-degree burglary as a class 3 felony, joining the two circumstances already elevated above the class 4 baseline. Covers burglary whose objective is the theft of one or more firearms or ammunition. Authorizes a fine of at least $5,000 and up to $750,000 in addition to any other sentence upon conviction. Makes the required 5-year statutory appropriation.

bills.title: Extreme Risk Protection Orders
bills.summary: Creates a process for a family or household member or a law enforcement officer to petition a court for a temporary extreme risk protection order. Requires the petitioner to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the person poses a significant risk to self or others by having a firearm in their custody or control or by acquiring one, backed by a sworn affidavit stating the supporting facts. Requires the temporary hearing in person or by telephone on the filing day or the next court day. Requires a second hearing within 7 days of the temporary order to decide whether a continuing order is warranted.
sponsors: Rep. Alec Garnett and Rep. Cole Wist

bills.title: Handgun Safety Training For School Employees
bills.summary: Allows a county sheriff to provide a handgun safety training course to employees of public elementary, middle, junior high, or high schools who hold concealed handgun permits. Requires the sheriff to consult with each school district board of education, and the state charter school institute where applicable, in setting the curriculum. Requires the curriculum to account for existing emergency response frameworks and to satisfy insurability standards for armed school employees.

bills.title: Concealed Carry For Military Under Twenty-one Years Of Age
bills.summary: Existing law requires a concealed handgun permit applicant to be at least 21 years old. Amends the age requirement to accept applicants who are 18 or older and on active duty in, or honorably discharged from, any branch or reserve branch of the United States military, including the National Guard. Leaves the 21-year minimum in place for all other applicants.

bills.title: Repeal Ammunition Magazine Prohibition
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory provisions barring possession of certain ammunition magazines. Also repeals the requirement that covered magazines manufactured in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 bear a permanent stamp or marking of that manufacture date. Eliminates both provisions from state law.
sponsors: Sen. Marble, Rep. Humphrey, Rep. Saine

bills.title: Legalize Gravity Knives And Switchblades
bills.summary: Removes gravity knives and switchblade knives from the statutory definition of illegal weapon. Legalizes possession of those knives as a result. Leaves other categories of illegal weapons untouched.

bills.title: Concealed Carry In Public Schools
bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, restricts concealed handgun permit holders by prohibiting carry on public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school grounds. Removes that restriction. Keeps the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition unchanged.
sponsors: Rep. Neville, Rep. Ransom, Sen. Neville

bills.title: Deadly Force Against An Intruder At A Business
bills.summary: Extends the existing right to use deadly physical force against a person who makes an illegal entry, under certain conditions, to additional actors. Adds owners of businesses. Also adds managers and employees of businesses.

bills.title: Repeal Ammunition Magazine Prohibition
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory prohibition on possessing certain ammunition magazines. Also strikes the requirement that covered magazines manufactured in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 include a permanent stamp or marking showing that date. Removes both provisions from the code.
sponsors: Rep. Saine, Rep. Humphrey, Sen. Neville, Sen. Marble

bills.title: Deadly Force Against An Intruder At A Business

bills.title: Repeal Ammo Magazine Prohibition
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory prohibition on possessing large-capacity ammunition magazines. Also repeals the requirement that large-capacity magazines made in Colorado on or after July 1, 2013 carry a permanent stamp or marking of that manufacture date. Strikes both provisions from state law.
sponsors: Rep. Saine, Rep. Humphrey, Sen. Marble

bills.title: Concealed Carry For Military Personnel
bills.summary: Creates a new exemption to the offense of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon. Applies the exemption when the person is on active duty serving in the armed forces of the United States military. Limits the exemption to cases where the weapon is a concealed handgun.

bills.title: Allow Concealed Carry On Public School Grounds
bills.summary: Current law, with exceptions, limits concealed handgun permit holders by barring carry on the grounds of public elementary, middle, junior high, and high schools. Removes that limitation for permit holders. Preserves the existing exceptions to the school-grounds prohibition.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry Without Permit
bills.summary: Allows a law-abiding person to carry a concealed handgun without a permit. Preserves the current restrictions on carrying concealed handguns on certain property, including school grounds. Reduces an appropriation in connection with the change.

bills.title: Repeal Large Ammo Magazine Ban
bills.summary: Repeals the state restrictions on large-capacity ammunition magazines. Eliminates the associated requirements imposed on such magazines under those provisions. Strikes the provisions from state law.
sponsors: Sen. Marble, Rep. Saine & Rep. Humphrey

bills.title: Concealed Carry Weapon Permits For Military Personnel
bills.summary: Opens concealed handgun permits to military personnel who are younger than 21. Applies to members of the military who would otherwise satisfy the permit criteria. Leaves the 21-year age requirement in place for non-military applicants.

bills.title: No Governor Authority Over Firearms In Emergencies
bills.summary: Addresses the governor's authority over firearms during a state of disaster emergency. Removes the authority to restrict the distribution of firearms during such an emergency. Leaves other disaster-emergency powers unaffected.

bills.title: Mental Hlth Professional Disclosure School Safety
bills.summary: Current law generally bars mental health professionals from disclosing confidential client communications without consent. Creates an exception when the client makes an articulable and significant threat against a school or its occupants. Also creates an exception when the client exhibits behavior that, in the professional's reasonable judgment, creates an articulable and significant threat to students, teachers, administrators, or other school personnel. Limits any such disclosure to appropriate school or district personnel and law enforcement agencies, with the information otherwise kept confidential.

bills.title: Protection Endangered Animals Poaching Trafficking
bills.summary: Prohibits the sale, purchase, trade, or distribution of parts and products of covered animal species, with limited exceptions. Excludes guns, knives, and musical instruments from the prohibition. Establishes an unclassified misdemeanor for a first offense and an unclassified felony for second and subsequent offenses, each with monetary penalties. Authorizes Colorado wildlife officers and other commissioned officers of the wildlife division to enforce the provisions.

bills.title: Application For An Amendment-proposing Convention
bills.summary: Applies to the United States Congress to call a convention under Article V of the federal constitution. Limits the convention's sole agenda to proposing an amendment setting term limits for Congress. The contemplated amendment would cap the number of terms a person may be elected to the United States House of Representatives and to the United States Senate.

bills.title: Prohibit Forfeitures Without Criminal Conviction
bills.summary: Requires that a court may not enter a judgment of forfeiture of property unless an owner of the property has been convicted of the underlying offense, with limited exceptions such as a plea agreement, an owner who evades the court's jurisdiction, or a settlement agreed to by all parties. It gives the person whose property was seized the right to a pretrial hearing or a writ of replevin to challenge the validity of the seizure or to require return of the property, with the court granting relief when return is likely, the property is not needed for the investigation, or the property is the only means to pay for legal representation. The act also bars state law enforcement agencies from participating in a federal forfeiture action unless the seized property is worth more than fifty thousand dollars and requires that any federal forfeiture proceeds they receive be credited to the state general fund.

bills.title: Lift Restrictions On Carrying Of Firearms
bills.summary: Allows a person who is at least twenty-one years old and who legally possesses a handgun under state and federal law to carry a concealed handgun in Colorado without a permit. The authority created is equal in all respects to that granted by a concealed handgun permit, so the carrier has the same rights and is subject to the same limitations, including the prohibition on carrying on the grounds of a public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school. The act also makes corresponding adjustments to state appropriations, reducing funding for the bureau's identification unit and the instant criminal background check cash fund, and it takes effect upon passage.

bills.title: Repeal Gun Transfer Background Check Rqmnt & Fee
bills.summary: Repeals the requirement that a person who is not a licensed gun dealer must obtain a criminal background check of the transferee and the approval of the Colorado bureau of investigation before transferring possession of a firearm. It also repeals the bureau's fee for performing an instant criminal background check and the associated instant criminal background check cash fund. The act makes conforming changes to the civil protection order, protection order, and domestic violence sentencing statutes, and it adjusts state appropriations by shifting the cost of background checks from the cash fund to the general fund.

bills.title: Ammunition Magazines
bills.summary: Deletes the state's prohibitions on the possession of large-capacity magazines and the requirement that large-capacity magazines manufactured in Colorado carry identification markings. The change removes part 3 of article 12 of title 18 of the Colorado Revised Statutes, the part of the code that imposed those magazine rules. The act also carries a safety clause finding it necessary for the immediate preservation of public peace, health, and safety.
sponsors: Sen. Holbert, Sen. Cooke, Rep. Humphrey

bills.title: Repeal Large Ammo Magazine Ban
bills.summary: Repeals the statutory provisions that prohibit the possession of large-capacity ammunition magazines and that require identification markings to be placed on large-capacity magazines manufactured in the state. The act deletes part 3 of article 12 of title 18 of the Colorado Revised Statutes, the part of the code that contained those magazine restrictions. It includes a safety clause declaring the act necessary for the immediate preservation of public peace, health, and safety.

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruders In Businesses
bills.summary: Extends the right to use deadly physical force against an intruder beyond occupants of a dwelling to include owners, managers, and employees of a place of business. The force is justified when the person has made an unlawful entry and the owner, manager, or employee reasonably believes the intruder committed or intends to commit a crime and might use force, however slight, against anyone in the dwelling or business. A person acting under that authority is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act also makes the defense-of-premises statute gender-neutral and permits deadly force to prevent an attempted first degree arson.

bills.title: Repeal Gun Transfer Background Check Rqmnt & Fee
bills.summary: Repeals the requirement that a person who is not a licensed gun dealer must obtain a criminal background check of the transferee and the approval of the Colorado bureau of investigation before transferring possession of a firearm. It also repeals the bureau's fee for performing an instant criminal background check and the associated instant criminal background check cash fund. The act makes conforming changes to the civil protection order, protection order, and domestic violence sentencing statutes, replacing the prior receipt-and-background-check documentation with a single written receipt signed by both parties.

bills.title: CBI Produce Certificates For Gun Transferees
bills.summary: Requires the Colorado bureau of investigation to act within five days of a request for the certificate that federal law requires for transfers of machine guns, destructive devices, and certain other firearms. The bureau must either issue the certificate or deny it with a written explanation and an opportunity for the applicant to provide additional information. A denied applicant may seek judicial review, at which the bureau bears the burden of proving the applicant is ineligible by a preponderance of the evidence, and the court may award attorney fees to the prevailing party. When the bureau issues a certificate, it may not keep a record identifying the specific model or serial number of the firearm.
sponsors: Rep. P. Neville, Sen. T. Neville

bills.title: No Liability For Permitting Concealed Carry
bills.summary: Provides that the owner or operator of a place of business open to the public is not liable for damages in a civil action alleged to have resulted from the business adopting a policy that allows a person holding a concealed handgun permit to carry on its premises. The immunity applies only to businesses that adopt such a policy and does not affect the liability of other businesses or diminish rights available to them under existing law. The act takes effect on the day following the expiration of the ninety-day period after the general assembly's final adjournment, subject to a possible referendum petition.

bills.title: No Background Check Concealed Handgun Permittees
bills.summary: Allows a person holding a valid Colorado concealed handgun permit, issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2016, to satisfy the state and federal background check requirements for receiving a transferred firearm by presenting the permit and a valid government-issued identification card. The exemption applies whether the transferor is a gun show vendor or a licensed importer, manufacturer, or dealer. To make the permits verifiable, it requires the Colorado bureau of investigation to establish a uniform, tamper-resistant template that each sheriff must use when issuing permits on or after that date. It also adds citizenship and immigration details to the permit application so the application itself satisfies federal criminal background check requirements.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry No Permit
bills.summary: Allows a person who is at least twenty-one years old and who legally possesses a handgun under state and federal law to carry a concealed handgun in Colorado without a permit. The authority created is equal in all respects to that granted by a concealed handgun permit, so a person carrying under it has the same rights and is subject to the same limitations, including the prohibition on carrying on the grounds of a public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry In Public Schools
bills.summary: Removes the statutory prohibition that barred a person holding a valid concealed handgun permit from carrying a concealed handgun on the grounds of a public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school. Under the act, carrying a handgun on school grounds with a valid permit or temporary emergency permit is no longer an offense under the unlawful-carrying-on-school-grounds statute. The change applies to the real property of the school and any improvements erected on it, effectively treating school grounds like other public property for permit holders.

bills.title: No Disorderly Conduct For Blanks Fired At Funerals
bills.summary: Clarifies that the ritual discharge of blank ammunition cartridges at a funeral for a deceased veteran of the armed forces of the United States does not constitute the criminal offense of disorderly conduct. The change adds that exception to the provision making it disorderly conduct to discharge a firearm in a public place, which already excludes lawful target practice and hunting. It therefore allows funeral attendees to fire blanks in honor of a fallen service member without risking a disorderly conduct charge.

bills.title: Sales & Use Tax Holiday Firearms Ammo Accessories
bills.summary: Creates a state sales and use tax exemption for firearms, ammunition, and firearm accessories sold on the first Friday and Saturday of August in 2014, 2015, and 2016. The exemption applies only to sales by a vendor that elects to participate for a given year, and a participating vendor may not apply the exemption selectively to only some of its sales. Firearm accessories are defined to include replacement parts and attachments as well as items used to carry or store a firearm, such as stocks, scopes, grips, magazines, cases, and holsters. A town, city, or county may adopt an identical local sales tax exemption for the same periods.

bills.title: Restoration Of Firearm Carry Right For Some Felons
bills.summary: Creates a court process that allows a person convicted of certain nonviolent felonies to petition for restoration of the right to possess and carry a firearm after a five-year waiting period following completion of the sentence. The sentencing court may issue a certificate of restoration if, by a preponderance of the evidence, the petitioner has a lawful occupation or source of income, has had no new convictions and no pending charges, has shown lawful and substantial reasons, and poses no unreasonable risk to public safety. Eligibility is limited to a specified list of nonviolent offenses, excluding arson, certain burglaries, and robbery, and a denied petitioner may not refile for at least one year. The district attorney must notify the victim of the petition.

bills.title: Governor Cannot Restrict Firearms During Emergency
bills.summary: Removes the governor's authority to suspend or limit the sale, dispensing, or transportation of firearms during a state of disaster emergency. The change strips firearms from the list of items the governor may restrict in an emergency, which continues to cover alcoholic beverages, explosives, and combustibles. The act takes effect on the day following the expiration of the ninety-day period after the general assembly's final adjournment, subject to a possible referendum petition.

bills.title: No Background Check For Step-relations
bills.summary: Expands the existing exceptions to the private firearms transfer background check requirement so that they also cover transfers between step-relatives. The first exception, for a bona fide gift or loan between immediate family members such as spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, nieces, nephews, first cousins, aunts, and uncles, is broadened to include the step-relatives of those persons. The second exception, which covers a member of the armed forces who will be deployed outside the country within thirty days transferring to an immediate family member, is likewise extended to include a step-relative of that person.

bills.title: Background Checks And Fees For Gun Transfers
bills.summary: Repeals the statute that required a person who is not a licensed gun dealer to obtain a criminal background check of the transferee and the approval of the Colorado bureau of investigation before transferring possession of a firearm. It also repeals the bureau's fee for performing an instant criminal background check and the associated instant criminal background check cash fund. The repealed statute had contained a broad list of transfer exceptions, including gifts between immediate family members, transfers by operation of law or at death, and temporary transfers at ranges, competitions, and during hunting.

bills.title: Clean-up SB13-250 Drug Sentencing
bills.summary: Makes conforming corrections to the drug sentencing provisions adopted by a prior 2013 measure so that the statute's internal references and definitions line up with the new drug offense levels. It clarifies that the terms misdemeanor and petty offense include the corresponding drug offenses, that offenses may fall into one of six drug offense levels, and that level 1 or 2 drug felonies carry the same preliminary hearing and alternate juror rights as class 1, 2, or 3 felonies. It also corrects an internal cross-reference so that the vacatur of certain level 4 drug felony convictions applies to the offenses actually described in the code.

bills.title: School Board Policies Allowing Concealed Carry
bills.summary: Permits a school district board of education and the governing board of a charter or institute charter school to adopt a written policy allowing an employee of the district or school to carry a concealed handgun within its buildings and on its grounds. Such a policy may apply only to an employee who holds a valid concealed handgun carry permit, and the board may add requirements, such as training, on top of the permit. The bill creates matching exceptions to the rule that otherwise prohibits carrying a concealed handgun on public school property, letting a permittee who is a district or charter-school employee carry in accordance with the board's adopted policy. Adoption of such a policy is discretionary, so each board decides whether to authorize employee carry on its own campuses.
sponsors: Sen. Renfroe, Sen. Harvey, Rep. Saine

bills.title: Require Security At No-firearms Businesses
bills.summary: Creates civil liability for a private business that bans firearms on its premises but does not provide proportionate armed security. A business becomes liable for damages in a suit brought by an invitee when it holds itself open to the public, prohibits the carrying of firearms—concealed or open—where that carrying would otherwise be lawful, and fails to staff at least one on-duty security officer armed with a firearm for every fifty people present. The invitee must also show that the resulting injuries stemmed from another person's actions that the invitee could have resisted with a firearm had the business not imposed the ban. The term private business entity is defined to include tax-exempt not-for-profit organizations that conduct retail sales or provide retail services to the public.

bills.title: Modify Definition Of Deadly Weapon
bills.summary: Revises the statutory definition of a deadly weapon so that the category of any other weapon, device, instrument, material, or substance that is capable of producing death or serious bodily injury is brought within the same definitional clause as firearms and knives. The change folds the separate bludgeon and catch-all subparts into a single provision covering any animate or inanimate object that, in the manner it is used or intended to be used, is capable of producing death or serious bodily injury. It does not add or remove any specific object from the definition but restructures how the definition is organized.
sponsors: Rep. Mike Foote, Sen. Rollie Heath

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruder At A Business
bills.summary: Extends the right to use deadly physical force against an intruder, which previously applied only to occupants of dwellings, so that owners, managers, and employees of a place of business may also use any degree of force, including deadly force, against a person who has made an unlawful entry into the business. The protection applies when the owner, manager, or employee reasonably believes the intruder committed or intends to commit a crime beyond the uninvited entry and might use any physical force, however slight, against a person on the premises. A person using force in accordance with these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The measure also updates the related defense-of-premises statute with gender-neutral language.

bills.title: Change Possession Of Weapons By Previous Offender
bills.summary: Narrows the crime of possession of a weapon by a previous offender, which under existing law applied to any prior felony conviction, so that it now reaches only specific categories of felonies. A person commits the offense if they knowingly possess, use, or carry a firearm or other covered weapon after a conviction for a felony defined in the victim's rights act, for burglary or arson, or for any felony involving the use of force or a deadly weapon, including attempt or conspiracy to commit such a felony. The same narrowed scope applies to juvenile adjudications for conduct that would be a felony if committed by an adult, and the required written statement given at sentencing is updated to reflect the changed list of offenses. The changes apply to offenses committed on or after July 1, 2013.

bills.title: No Background Check With Concealed Carry Permit
bills.summary: Allows a valid Colorado concealed handgun carry permit to stand in for the otherwise-required criminal background check when a firearm changes hands, so a transferee who presents the permit and a valid government-issued photo ID is exempt from the instant criminal background check. The exemption applies to transfers at gun shows and to licensed firearm dealers, who are relieved of the duty to contact the state point of contact or the national instant criminal background check system before the transfer. To make the permit a reliable substitute, the measure requires the bureau of investigation to issue a uniform, tamper-resistant permit template and to run a national background check on each applicant's fingerprints, and it adds citizenship and immigration questions to the permit application. The background-check exemption applies only to permits issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2014.

bills.title: No Federal Laws Concerning Colorado Firearms
bills.summary: Prohibits state employees, agents, and agencies—including peace officers—from enforcing any federal law that touches a firearm, ammunition, magazine, or accessory manufactured in the United States and kept entirely within Colorado's borders. A federal statute, rule, or regulation taking effect on or after January 1, 2013 is likewise unenforceable in the state if it would ban or restrict ownership of a semi-automatic firearm or magazine, require registration of a firearm or accessory, or restrict purchases by Colorado residents or visiting out-of-state residents. The attorney general may defend a Colorado resident prosecuted by the federal government over such an item when it was made or bought in Colorado and never left the state. A federal employee or agent who enforces or attempts to enforce a covered law commits a class 1 misdemeanor.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry No Permit
bills.summary: Creates a permitless option for carrying a concealed handgun in Colorado by allowing a person who is at least twenty-one years old and legally possesses a handgun under state and federal law to carry it concealed without first obtaining a permit. The authority granted is equal in all respects to a concealed handgun carry permit, so the carrier has the same rights and is subject to the same limitations, including the prohibition on carrying a concealed handgun on the grounds of a public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school. The change is made to the unlawful-carrying statute and to the parallel statute covering school, college, and university grounds, so that qualifying possession is not treated as an offense. The provision applies to offenses committed on or after the act takes effect.

bills.title: Policies Allowing Concealed Carry In Public School
bills.summary: Authorizes a school district board of education and the governing board of a charter or institute charter school to adopt a written policy permitting an employee of the district or school to carry a concealed handgun within its buildings and on its grounds. The policy may only apply to an employee who holds a valid concealed handgun carry permit, and the governing board may impose additional conditions, such as completing training, beyond holding the permit. The bill adds corresponding exceptions to the statute that otherwise bars carrying a concealed handgun on public school property, so a permittee who is a district or charter-school employee may carry in line with the board-adopted policy. The authority is discretionary, leaving each board to decide whether and under what rules to allow such carry.

bills.title: No New Federal Firearm Laws
bills.summary: Declares that a federal statute, order, rule, or regulation taking effect on or after January 1, 2013 is unenforceable within Colorado if it would impose a prohibition, restriction, or limitation on the possession of a firearm, firearm accessory, or ammunition that does not exist under state law, including capacity or size limits and registration requirements. A federal employee or agent who enforces or attempts to enforce such a measure in violation of the prohibition commits a class 1 misdemeanor. The attorney general is authorized to defend a Colorado resident who is prosecuted by the federal government for an alleged offense under an unenforceable measure. The section also defines the covered terms, treating a firearm accessory as an item used with or mounted on a firearm, including a detachable ammunition magazine.

bills.title: No Concealed Carry At Colleges
bills.summary: Bars a concealed handgun permit holder from carrying a concealed handgun on the campus of a public institution of higher education, covering any building or structure the institution uses for any purpose, any stadium or arena it uses to host events, and any outdoor institution-sponsored event where the campus chief administrator, in consultation with the campus safety chief, has chosen to prohibit firearms. A permittee who is employed or retained by contract by the institution as a security officer remains permitted to carry while on duty. The measure updates the unlawful-carrying statutes so that carrying a concealed handgun in violation of the new campus restriction is a criminal offense. It defines a public institution of higher education to include colleges, universities, community and technical colleges, junior colleges, and area vocational schools.

bills.title: Background Checks For Gun Transfers
bills.summary: Requires a person who is not a licensed gun dealer to route a private firearm transfer through a licensed dealer so that a criminal background check is run on the prospective recipient and the bureau approves the transfer before possession may change hands. The unlicensed transferor arranges for the dealer to perform the check, the dealer records the transaction and may charge a fee of up to ten dollars, and the resulting approval is valid for thirty days. A transferor who makes a transfer in violation of these rules can be held jointly and severally liable for civil damages caused by the recipient's later use of the firearm. The law carves out exemptions for antique and curio-relic firearms, family gifts and loans, estate transfers, temporary transfers for self-defense or at ranges and while hunting, repair or maintenance, and transfers from service members about to deploy, and a violation is a class 1 misdemeanor carrying a two-year ban on possessing firearms.
sponsors: Rep. Rhonda Fields, Sen. Morgan Carroll

bills.title: Mental Health Task Force
bills.summary: Creates a thirty-member mental health and firearms task force to advise the legislature on the loss, maintenance, and restoration of the right to purchase and possess firearms by people who, because of mental health issues, alcohol or substance abuse, or family dynamics, are clearly dangerous to themselves or others. Members are appointed by a mix of legislators, the governor's office, the state court administrator, gun-safety and firearms-owner advocates, and the executive director of the behavioral health department, drawing on mental health clinicians, law enforcement, and affected family members. The task force holds public meetings, may take testimony and written comments, must meet at least five times, and is to deliver a written report of findings and recommendations to the house and senate judiciary committees by January 15, 2015. Members serve without pay or expense reimbursement, and the task force authority sunsets on August 1, 2015.

bills.title: No Firearms For Domestic Violence Offenders
bills.summary: Requires a court that subjects a person to a qualifying civil or mandatory criminal domestic violence protection order to order that person to refrain from possessing or purchasing any firearm or ammunition for the duration of the order and to relinquish any firearm or ammunition in their immediate possession or control. The relinquishment must occur within twenty-four hours of service in open court or forty-eight hours after service outside the court, with a court-authorized extension to seventy-two hours for a firearm or five days for ammunition if the person shows they cannot comply sooner. A person may satisfy the requirement by selling or transferring the items to a licensed dealer, arranging storage with a law enforcement agency, or transferring them to a private party who may legally possess them, and must file a receipt or written statement with the court within three business days. Violating the order by possessing or purchasing a firearm or ammunition, or failing to file the required proof, is a crime; the court must then issue a warrant for the person's arrest.
sponsors: Sen. Evie Hudak, Rep. Beth McCann

bills.title: No On-line Training For Concealed Handgun Permits
bills.summary: Requires an applicant for a concealed handgun carry permit to complete a handgun training class in person, excluding any firearms safety course that can be finished entirely over the internet or on an electronic device or in any location other than the physical place where the certified instructor offers the course. The applicant must submit a training certificate, original or a photocopy bearing the instructor's original signature, obtained within the ten years before the application is filed. The change clarifies that, to the extent permitted by the definition of a handgun training class, the applicant has discretion in choosing which qualifying class to complete. The measure takes effect upon the date of its approval and applies to permit applications submitted after that date.
sponsors: Sen. Lois Tochtrop, Rep. Jenise May

bills.title: Payment For Background Checks For Gun Transfers
bills.summary: Requires the bureau of investigation to charge a fee for performing the instant criminal background check that precedes a firearm transfer, capped at the bureau's total direct and indirect costs of conducting the check. All money collected is credited to a newly created instant criminal background check cash fund, which is subject to annual appropriation and whose unspent balances may be carried forward to reduce the fee in later periods. The bureau may contract with a public or private entity to collect the fee and must report to the Joint Budget Committee each January on the number of full-time employees it uses for background checks and on the calculations behind the fee. The measure also adjusts the general fund appropriations for the department of public safety to reflect the shift to a user-funded model.
sponsors: Rep. Lois Court, Sen. Rollie Heath

bills.title: Prohibiting Large-capacity Ammunition Magazines
bills.summary: Prohibits the sale, transfer, or possession of a large-capacity ammunition magazine beginning July 1, 2013, and defines the term to cover devices that hold more than fifteen rounds, tubular shotgun magazines holding more than twenty-eight inches of shells, or detachable non-tubular magazines holding more than eight shells when combined with a fixed magazine. Violating the prohibition is a class 2 misdemeanor, rising to a class 1 misdemeanor after a prior conviction and to a class 6 felony if the magazine is possessed during a felony or a crime of violence. A person who owned a qualifying magazine on the effective date and maintains continuous possession may still lawfully possess it, with the prosecution bearing the burden of refuting that claim. The law also requires magazines manufactured in Colorado on or after the effective date to carry a permanent identifying stamp and sets out exemptions for manufacturers, licensed dealers, and certain government and military personnel.
sponsors: Rep. Rhonda Fields, Sen. Mary Hodge

bills.title: Assault Weapon Responsibility Act
bills.summary: Creates a civil liability regime that treats an assault weapon—defined as any firearm other than a handgun, shotgun, or bolt-action rifle—as a dangerous product. A person who discharges such a weapon is strictly liable for all injuries and damages the discharge causes, with a narrow exception for defensive discharge inside a dwelling against an imminent threat to an occupant. Owners and possessors are liable for a third party's discharge if they negligently stored the weapon or let another take possession, and sellers, transferors, distributors, and manufacturers face liability for negligent entrustment or for sales made in knowing violation of state or federal law. The act also lets an owner surrender a weapon to law enforcement or a licensed dealer as an affirmative defense, requires the highest degree of care in handling these firearms, and repeals the statutes that shield firearm and ammunition manufacturers from certain civil suits.
sponsors: Sen. John Morse, Rep. Beth McCann

bills.title: Secret Service Peace Officer Authority
bills.summary: Designates certain United States Secret Service employees—special agents, uniform division officers, physical security technicians and specialists, and special officers—as limited peace officers within Colorado. They hold that status only when responding to a non-federal felony or misdemeanor committed in their presence, responding to an emergency requiring immediate action, assisting at the request of a Colorado peace officer, or acting as part of a joint task force or investigation with state officers, and only while following their agency's rules. After making an arrest under this authority, the agent must immediately hand the arrested person over to a Colorado peace officer. The provision does not waive the state's sovereign immunity, create an indemnification duty, or expand federal authority to open independent investigations into violations of Colorado law.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry With No Permit
bills.summary: Creates an exception to the offense of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon for a person who is at least twenty-one years old, legally possesses a handgun under state and federal law, and whose weapon involved in the incident was a handgun. A person carrying under the exception has the same carrying rights and is subject to the same limitations as a person who holds a concealed handgun carry permit. The bill also adds a parallel exception to the offense of possessing a weapon on school, college, or university grounds for the same class of lawful handgun possessors. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.
sponsors: Sen. Tim Neville, Rep. Randy Baumgardner

bills.title: End CBI Instacheck Duty For Firearm Transfers
bills.summary: Relieves the Colorado bureau of investigation of its statutory duty to act as the state point of contact for the national instant criminal background check system in firearm transfer cases, so that gun show vendors and sheriffs must instead contact the federal bureau of investigation directly to complete the required background checks. The measure makes conforming changes to the gun show transfer rule, the concealed handgun permit verification process, and the temporary emergency permit process so each references the federal system rather than the bureau. It also updates the theft-of-medical-records statute to keep access to medical information through the background check system outside the definition of theft. The bill reduces the bureau's and the department of public safety's appropriations to reflect the elimination of the state-run check program.

bills.title: Firearm Possession During State Of Emergency
bills.summary: Prohibits the state or any political subdivision, during a declared state of emergency, from prohibiting or restricting the otherwise lawful possession, use, carrying, transfer, transportation, storage, or display of a firearm or ammunition, from seizing or confiscating a lawfully possessed firearm except in defined circumstances such as self-defense, an arrest, or seizure as evidence, or from requiring registration of a firearm or ammunition for which registration is not otherwise required by law. An exception allows restrictions on the commercial sale of firearms or ammunition when an authorized authority has ordered an evacuation or a general closure of businesses in the affected area. An individual whose rights are violated may bring a civil action for damages against any person who subjects them to a prohibited action, and may also sue for the return of a seized firearm or ammunition. A prevailing plaintiff in any action to enforce the provision is awarded costs and reasonable attorney fees.
sponsors: Rep. Amy Stephens, Sen. Steve King

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruder At Place Of Business
bills.summary: Extends the existing justification for using lethal force against an intruder to cover places of business in addition to dwellings. An owner, manager, or employee of a business may use any degree of force, including lethal force, against a person who makes an unlawful entry into the business when the person has a reasonable belief the intruder has committed or intends to commit a crime in the business and might use any physical force, however slight, against an occupant. A person using force under these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act also updates the defense-of-premises provision to permit lethal force under the new business-intruder circumstances and takes effect after the ninety-day referendum-petition period.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry Without Permit
bills.summary: Creates an exception to the offenses of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon and of possessing a weapon on school, college, or university grounds for a person who is at least twenty-one years old, may legally possess a handgun under state and federal law, and is carrying a handgun. Under the exception, the person's authority to carry a concealed handgun is equal in all respects to the authority granted by a concealed handgun carry permit, including the same rights and the same limitations. The exception does not allow carrying a concealed handgun on the real property of a public school district, and the existing restriction on carrying on the real property of public elementary, middle, junior high, or high schools continues to apply. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Exception
bills.summary: Creates an exception to the offense of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon for a person who is at least twenty-one years old, may legally possess a handgun under state and federal law, and whose weapon involved in the incident was a handgun. Under the exception, the person's authority to carry a concealed handgun is equal in all respects to the authority granted by a concealed handgun carry permit, with the same rights and the same limitations. The bill also adds a matching exception to the offense of possessing a weapon on school, college, or university grounds for the same class of lawful handgun possessors. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Deadly Force Against A Business Intruder
bills.summary: Extends the justification for using lethal force against an intruder to cover places of business in addition to dwellings. An owner, manager, or employee of a business may use any degree of force, including lethal force, against a person who makes an unlawful entry into the business when the person reasonably believes the intruder has committed or intends to commit a crime in the business and might use any physical force, however slight, against an occupant. A person using force under these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act also updates the defense-of-premises provision so that lethal force is permitted under the new business-intruder circumstances, and it takes effect after the ninety-day referendum-petition period.

bills.title: Governor Disaster Authority Firearms
bills.summary: Removes firearms from the list of items the governor may suspend or limit the sale, dispensing, or transportation of during a state of disaster emergency. The governor retains the same authority over alcoholic beverages, explosives, and combustibles. The act takes effect at the start of the day following the expiration of the ninety-day referendum-petition period after final adjournment of the general assembly.

bills.title: Peace Officer Status US Marshals
bills.summary: Designates a deputy or special deputy United States marshal as a peace officer under the state's federal special agent provision, alongside special agents of the federal bureau of investigation, the bureau of alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and explosives, and officers of the federal protective service of immigration and customs enforcement. The designated officers may act when responding to a nonfederal felony or misdemeanor committed in their presence, responding to an emergency where immediate action is required to prevent escape, serious bodily injury, or property destruction, rendering assistance at the request of a Colorado peace officer, or working in a bona fide task force or joint investigation with Colorado peace officers. After effecting an arrest under the section, the officer must immediately surrender custody of the arrested individual to a Colorado peace officer. The section does not expand the authority of federal officers to initiate or conduct an independent investigation of state law violations and does not impose state liability or waive sovereign immunity.

bills.title: Removal of Emergency Firearms Ban
bills.summary: Removes firearms from the list of items the governor may suspend or limit the sale, dispensing, or transportation of during a state of disaster emergency. The governor retains the same authority over alcoholic beverages, explosives, and combustibles. The act takes effect at the start of the day following the expiration of the ninety-day referendum-petition period after final adjournment of the general assembly.
sponsors: Sen. Scott Renfroe / Rep. Jerry Sonnenberg

bills.title: Firearms Freedom Act
bills.summary: Declares that a personal firearm, firearm accessory, or ammunition manufactured commercially or privately in Colorado by a person who is not federally licensed and that remains within the state is not subject to federal law or regulation, including registration, under Congress's interstate commerce authority. The exemption requires that the words 'Made in Colorado' be clearly stamped on a central metallic part of the firearm, such as the receiver or frame. The exemption does not apply to a firearm that cannot be carried and used by one person, a firearm with a bore diameter greater than one and one-half inches that uses smokeless powder, ammunition with a projectile that explodes after leaving the firearm, or a firearm other than a shotgun that discharges two or more projectiles with one activation of the trigger. The act applies to firearms, accessories, and ammunition manufactured in Colorado on or after its effective date, which follows the ninety-day referendum-petition period.
sponsors: Sen. Dave Schultheis / Rep. Steve King

bills.title: Make My Day Better – Businesses
bills.summary: Extends the right to use lethal force against an intruder to owners, managers, and employees of places of business as well as occupants of dwellings. The justification applies when a person makes an unlawful entry into the business and the owner, manager, or employee reasonably believes the intruder has committed or intends to commit a crime there and might use any physical force, however slight, against an occupant. A person using force under these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act also updates the defense-of-premises provision to allow lethal force under the new business-intruder circumstances and takes effect after the ninety-day referendum-petition period.
sponsors: Rep. Cory Gardner, Sen. Ted Harvey

bills.title: No Brady for Permit Holders
bills.summary: Exempts a person who holds a valid concealed handgun carry permit issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2010 from the instant criminal background check requirement when receiving a firearm transfer, so long as the person presents the permit and a valid identification card issued by a federal or state agency. The exemption covers transfers at gun shows and transfers by licensed firearm importers, manufacturers, and dealers. The act also requires sheriffs to issue permits conforming to a uniform template established by the bureau of investigation, requires permit applications to include the applicant's country of citizenship, and requires the bureau to search the national instant criminal background check system when processing permit fingerprints.

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruder Businesses
bills.summary: Extends the justification for using lethal force against an intruder to cover places of business in addition to dwellings. An owner, manager, or employee of a business may use any degree of force, including lethal force, against a person who makes an unlawful entry into the business when the person reasonably believes the intruder has committed or intends to commit a crime there and might use any physical force, however slight, against an occupant. A person using force under these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act also updates the defense-of-premises provision so that lethal force is permitted under the new business-intruder circumstances.
sponsors: Sen. Ted Harvey, Rep. Cory Gardner

bills.title: Heller Enforcement
bills.summary: Prohibits a local government from enacting an ordinance, regulation, or other law that requires a person to store a firearm in a manner that renders it inoperable, including by disassembly or use of a trigger-lock device. Any such local law in place before the effective date of the prohibition is void and unenforceable. The act also permits a Colorado firearms manufacturer to sell a firearm or accessory manufactured in the state to a Colorado resident, and permits a Colorado resident to purchase such an item, regardless of any contrary federal law. The provisions of the act are severable.

bills.title: Access To Firearms By Minors
bills.summary: Creates the crime of criminal storage of a firearm when a person keeps a firearm on premises under his or her custody or control, knows or reasonably should know that a minor could access it without a parent's or guardian's permission, the minor obtains access, and the minor uses the firearm to cause death or bodily injury to himself, herself, or another person or carries it to a school or school-sponsored event. The offense is an unclassified misdemeanor punishable by a fine of fifty to one thousand dollars, credited to the suicide prevention coordination cash fund. Exceptions apply when the minor acts in self-defense or defense of the residence, is under direct parental supervision during safety courses, target practice, hunting, or organized competitions, or when the firearm is locked, stored securely, or kept apart from its ammunition. The act also requires licensed gun dealers to deliver a written storage warning with each firearm sale or transfer and to post it at each purchase counter, and requires gun show promoters to post the warning at each entrance.

bills.title: Stand Your Ground/Make My Day Better
bills.summary: Extends the justification for using lethal force against an intruder to places of business as well as dwellings. An occupant of a dwelling or place of business may use any degree of force, including lethal force, against a person who makes an unlawful entry when the occupant reasonably believes the intruder has committed or intends to commit a crime in the premises and might use any physical force, however slight, against any occupant. A person using force under these conditions is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the force. The act takes effect on the day following the expiration of the ninety-day referendum-petition period after final adjournment of the general assembly.
sponsors: Rep. Cary Gardner, Sen. Ted Harvey

bills.title: Prohibit Vehicles On Public Lands
bills.summary: Makes it unlawful for a person to operate a motor vehicle on any federal public land, trail, or road unless the land, trail, or road is signed or otherwise authorized for such use by the controlling land management agency. Enforcement does not commence within an administrative unit until the controlling agency identifies available routes by maps, route markers, or signs available to the public. A violation is a misdemeanor punishable by a one hundred dollar fine, or two hundred dollars within a federal wilderness area, with additional license suspension points when the person was hunting, fishing, or trapping at the time. The prohibition does not apply to peace officers on duty, persons acting at their direction, or persons authorized by legal right or agency permission, including administrative or emergency access, facility maintenance, ski area, oil and gas, or logging operations, and the provision is repealed effective July 1, 2013.
sponsors: Rep. Kathleen Curry, Sen. Lois Tochtrop

bills.title: No Hunting “confined” Animals
bills.summary: Makes it unlawful for a person to offer another person the opportunity to hunt, wound, or take any mammal that is intentionally confined in an enclosure, regardless of size, or intentionally tied, staked, caged, or otherwise restrained from engaging in normal movement. Exceptions allow taking a mammal at a slaughtering establishment for meat, leather, or fur production and humanely euthanizing a mammal for health, safety, or scientific purposes. A violation involving big game or an endangered species is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of ten thousand to twenty-five thousand dollars and suspension of wildlife license privileges for a minimum of one year to life, while a violation involving any other mammal is a misdemeanor punishable by a one hundred to one thousand dollar fine and twenty hunting license suspension points.

bills.title: Close Down Sunday Gun Sales
bills.summary: Removes the requirement that the bureau of investigation remain open for business at least twelve hours per day, every calendar day except Christmas and Thanksgiving, in order to transmit background check requests to the national instant criminal background check system and search other databases. Instead, the bureau must be open during the minimum hours specified for point-of-contact agencies in the federal system's user manual. The bureau must continue to provide a toll-free telephone number operational every day the office is open and must monitor and evaluate call volumes while staffing its background check unit at levels that ensure prompt processing. The legislative findings state that the change would let the bureau concentrate staff during peak call volumes to reduce dealer wait times.
sponsors: Rep. Jim Kerr, Sen. Jack Taylor

bills.title: Regul Political Telephone Solicitations
bills.summary: Prohibits a political telephone caller from making a political telephone solicitation to any person located in Colorado or registered to vote in the state unless the caller has a preexisting relationship with the person, such as a voluntary declaration of party affiliation or prior consent to receive future solicitations. A political telephone solicitation is an unsolicited call made by an automatic dialing-announcing device or a paid person expressing support for or opposition to a candidate, ballot issue, or political cause, requesting a donation, or inviting the recipient to take part in a poll or reveal voting intent. Bona fide candidates, candidate committees, incumbents, and political parties are exempt when calling existing constituents or supporters solely to announce a town meeting, fund-raiser, or other event of interest, between 9 in the morning and 8 in the evening. A violation is a class 1 misdemeanor, and unlawful solicitations to cellular telephones also expose the caller to a private civil action for consequential damages, court costs, attorney fees, and a statutory penalty.

bills.title: Gun-Free Zones Liability
bills.summary: Creates a private right of action for a person injured as a result of criminal conduct that occurs in a gun-free zone, allowing the person to sue the person, organization, entity, or government agency that created the zone for damages. The plaintiff must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that a reasonable person would believe possession of a firearm could have helped the plaintiff defend himself or herself against the criminal conduct. Treble damages apply if a terrorist attack caused the conduct or the plaintiff is disabled, over sixty-five years old, or a member of a racial or ethnic minority group. The covered crimes include murder, first or second degree assault, kidnapping, sexual offenses, aggravated robbery, first degree arson, and first degree burglary, committed with the use or threatened use of a lethal weapon, and a zone that provides reasonable security measures such as armed guards or metal detectors is not liable.

bills.title: Reciprocity Concealed Weapons Permits
bills.summary: Clarifies the residency requirements for reciprocity of concealed weapons permits issued by other states. For an out-of-state permit to carry a concealed handgun or concealed weapon to be valid in Colorado, the holder must be at least 21 years old and must be either a resident of the issuing state, as shown by the address on a valid picture identification issued by that state, or a resident of Colorado for no more than 90 days. The statute defines a valid picture identification as a driver's license or a state identification card.

bills.title: Repeal Permit Holder in Criminal Database
bills.summary: Prohibits the creation and maintenance of a statewide database of concealed handgun permit holders. Sheriffs may still share permittee information with other law enforcement agencies, but only to verify the validity of a specific permit, and any database that includes permittees must be searchable only by name. The bill requires that any permittee information already in a statewide database be removed immediately, and no later than July 1, 2007.

bills.title: Deadly Force Against Intruder
bills.summary: Extends the presumption justifying deadly physical force against an intruder to places of business in addition to dwellings. An occupant of a dwelling or place of business is justified in using any degree of force, including deadly force, against a person who has made an unlawful entry and whom the occupant reasonably believes has committed, or intends to commit, a crime against a person or property. The occupant who uses such force in accordance with the statute is immune from criminal prosecution and from civil liability for injuries or death resulting from the use of force.

bills.title: Permit Holder in Criminal Database Permanent
bills.summary: Removes the statutory bar that prevents sheriffs from sharing concealed handgun permittee information to build a statewide database, making the database a permanent part of the permit system. It also adds a use restriction: a peace officer may not rely on the permittee database alone, without additional information, to establish reasonable suspicion for a traffic stop. The officer likewise may not use the database by itself to justify probable cause for a search or seizure of a person, a vehicle, or property.

bills.title: Give FBI/BATFE Agents New Powers
bills.summary: Grants limited peace officer authority to special agents of the federal bureau of investigation and the bureau of alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and explosives while they are in Colorado. Such an agent may act when responding to a nonfederal crime committed in the agent's presence, handling an emergency, assisting at the request of a Colorado peace officer, or participating in a bona fide task force or joint investigation with Colorado officers. Any person the agent arrests must be turned over immediately to a Colorado peace officer, and the authority does not let the agent initiate or conduct an independent investigation into violations of state law.

bills.title: Stand Your Ground
bills.summary: Extends the presumption justifying deadly physical force against an intruder to places of temporary lodging and occupied vehicles in addition to dwellings. Under the presumption, an occupant using force intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily harm is deemed to have held a reasonable fear of imminent peril when the intruder was unlawfully and forcibly entering the location, or was removing another person against their will. The presumption does not apply when the person has a lawful right to be in the location, when the person is a child or grandchild in the occupant's custody, or when the occupant is engaged in unlawful activity. An occupant acting under the statute is immune from criminal prosecution and civil liability.
sponsors: Rep. Cory Gardner, Sen. Doug Lamborn

bills.title: CCW Permit To Satisfy Brady Check
bills.summary: Exempts a gun show transferee who holds and presents a valid Colorado concealed handgun permit from the background check normally required before a firearm is transferred at a gun show. It also requires the Colorado bureau of investigation, when processing a permit application, to search the federal instant criminal background check system and forward a set of fingerprints to the federal bureau. Finally, it sets out the citizenship and immigration documentation that a permit applicant must provide, limiting eligibility to United States citizens and legal aliens who submit the specified identifying information.

bills.title: Raise Hunting Fees
bills.summary: Increases a wide range of statutory hunting and fishing license fees and establishes a Colorado wildlife habitat stamp, priced at $10 when bought alone, $5 with a hunting or fishing license, and $200 as a lifetime stamp. Persons aged 19 or older must buy the stamp, or hold a lifetime version, when purchasing a hunting or fishing license other than a one-day license or before entering state wildlife areas. The bill also adds a 75-cent surcharge to each hunting and fishing license to fund the wildlife management public education advisory council and adjusts nonresident big game fees annually according to the consumer price index.

bills.title: Gun Show Background Check Clarifications
bills.summary: Narrows the gun show background check requirement by removing the phrase that would trigger the check when a vendor only attempts to transfer a firearm, so that the check applies to actual completed transfers. It repeals the statutory definition of a collection, which had covered a trade, barter, or in-kind exchange of firearms. The bill also clarifies the definition of a gun show and sets an effective date of July 1, 2005, applying the changes to firearm transfers initiated on or after that date.
sponsors: Rep. Cory Gardner, Sen. Doug Lamborn

bills.title: Peace Officer Impersonation
bills.summary: Escalates the offense of impersonating a peace officer to a class six felony and adds a new offense prohibiting a person from being in control of a vehicle that contains a red or blue light visible directly in front of the vehicle's center. The new light offense carries affirmative defenses for peace officers, vehicles expressly authorized by a chief of police or sheriff, volunteer firefighters and ambulance attendants holding a permit, and vendors who sell or exhibit such lamps. The bill also appropriates funds to the corrections system to cover the added cost of housing the additional offenders.

bills.title: Gun Show Background Check Clarifications
bills.summary: Narrows the gun show background check requirement by removing the phrase that would trigger the check when a vendor only attempts to transfer a firearm, so that the check applies to actual completed transfers. It repeals the statutory definition of a collection, which had covered a trade, barter, or in-kind exchange of firearms. The bill also clarifies the definition of a gun show and sets an effective date of July 1, 2004, applying the changes to firearm transfers completed on or after that date.

bills.title: Self Defense A Mitigating Factor In Sentencing
bills.summary: Allows a court to sentence a defendant convicted of second degree assault under the general sentencing guidelines rather than the mandatory sentence of the crime of violence statute when the assault occurred in specific circumstances. Those circumstances include the victim being unlawfully on the defendant's property at the time of the assault, or the defendant acting under a good-faith but mistaken belief in the need for self-defense or defense of a third person. The change applies to offenses committed on or after July 1, 2004.

bills.title: Abolish Statewide Database
bills.summary: Prohibits the creation and maintenance of a statewide database of concealed handgun permit holders. Sheriffs may still share permittee information with other law enforcement agencies, but only to verify the validity of a specific permit, and any database that includes permittees must be searchable only by name. The bill requires that any permittee information already in a statewide database be removed by July 1, 2004.

bills.title: Increase Hunting Permit Fees
bills.summary: Raises most statutory hunting and fishing license fees, other than nonresident big game license fees, and adjusts those nonresident big game fees annually according to the consumer price index for the Denver-Boulder-Greeley metropolitan area. It funds the wildlife management public education advisory council with a 75-cent surcharge on each hunting and fishing license and repeals the voluntary checkoff for donations to the council. The bill extends the repeal date of the council to July 1, 2009, and the act takes effect January 1, 2005.

bills.title: No SS# For Hunting Permit
bills.summary: Removes the requirement that the division of wildlife collect an applicant's social security number on a license application, unless the number is required by federal law or mandated as a condition of the state receiving federal funds. It also prohibits any license issued by the department of natural resources or an authorized agent from displaying the holder's social security number. The change applies to recreational and other licenses handled by the department.
sponsors: Rep. Lundberg, Rep. Schultheis, Sen. Cairns

bills.title: Alaska Law
bills.summary: Creates an exception to the offense of unlawfully carrying a concealed weapon for a person who may legally possess a firearm under the laws of Colorado and the United States, provided the weapon involved is a firearm. A person carrying a concealed handgun under this exception has the same rights and is subject to the same limitations as a person who holds a permit to carry a concealed handgun. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: “Safe” Storage of A Firearm
bills.summary: Creates a class 3 misdemeanor offense of negligent storage of a firearm, which occurs when a firearm owner or custodian, acting with criminal negligence, stores a firearm and it comes into the possession of a person under 18 who then discharges it, killing himself, herself, or another person. The offense does not apply if the juvenile obtained the firearm while under direct parental supervision, in self-defense, defending a residence, at a safety course or shooting range, hunting under a valid license, in an organized competition, traveling to or from such activities, or as a result of a robbery or burglary. The act takes effect July 1, 2004.

bills.title: Concealed Carry
bills.summary: Creates a statewide concealed-handgun permit system administered by county sheriffs, declaring the permitting and carrying of concealed handguns a matter of statewide concern. A sheriff must issue a five-year permit to any legal resident age 21 or older who is eligible to possess a firearm under state and federal law, is not subject to a restraining order or chronic alcohol or controlled-substance impairment, and demonstrates handgun competence through a training certificate, military service, or other listed means. The permit is effective throughout the state, and a permittee must carry it with photo identification and produce both on demand by a law enforcement officer. A person carrying a handgun in a private vehicle for lawful use or while hunting needs no permit, and the handgun is not treated as concealed.

bills.title: Prohibit Local Governments From Regulating Firearms/Preemption
bills.summary: Declares that carrying a weapon in a private automobile or other private conveyance for hunting or lawful protection of a person or property is a matter of statewide concern, regardless of how many jurisdictions the person travels through. No municipality, county, or city and county may enact or enforce any ordinance restricting that travel. The act also bars local governments from keeping records or databases of people who buy, transfer, exchange, or leave firearms for repair or consignment, and from prohibiting the sale, purchase, or possession of any firearm that state or federal law allows. Local governments may still ban open carrying in specific buildings or areas, provided they post signs at public entrances.

bills.title: Vermont-style Concealed Carry
bills.summary: Establishes a statewide concealed-handgun permit program in which a county sheriff must issue a permit to any Colorado resident age 21 or older who is eligible to possess a firearm under state and federal law, without requiring completion of a training course. Applicants submit a standardized application and a fee capped at fifty dollars, and the sheriff verifies eligibility through the bureau of investigation's search of the national instant criminal background check system and state records. The sheriff must approve or deny the application within fifteen days, and a denied applicant may seek judicial review. Permits are valid for five years and effective throughout the state, local laws may not restrict a permit holder's carrying, and reciprocity recognizes permits from states that recognize Colorado permits.

bills.title: Gunshow “Loophole” Changes
bills.summary: Tightens the definition of a gun show by requiring that the event be publicly advertised as a gun show and limiting the term to the facility or portion of the facility where the event is held and where at least three gun show vendors are present. It removes from the definition the references to the number of firearms and to parking areas, and it repeals the definition of a collection. The bill also expands the definition of a gun show vendor to include a person who attempts to sell, transfer, or exchange a firearm at a gun show, and defines transfer and transferee to match federal law.

bills.title: Self-Defense as a Criminal Defense
bills.summary: Requires a court, in a criminal case where the defendant is not entitled to a jury instruction on self-defense as an affirmative defense, to allow the defendant to present relevant evidence that he or she was acting in self-defense. If the defendant presents such evidence, the court must give a self-defense law instruction and tell the jury it may consider the evidence in determining whether the defendant acted recklessly, with extreme indifference, or in a criminally negligent manner. The instruction is not an affirmative defense, the prosecutor bears no burden of disproving self-defense, and the provision does not apply to strict liability crimes.

bills.title: Declarations of States of Emergency
bills.summary: Adds a condition of riot, insurrection, or invasion to the statutory definition of a disaster for purposes of declaring a state of emergency. It repeals the provisions that let the governor prohibit the purchase, manufacture, receipt, carrying, use, sale, transport, or disposal of firearms and ammunition during such a condition, as well as the permit scheme and the penalty for violating it. The change folds the emergency firearms restrictions into the general disaster declaration framework.

bills.title: Brady-NICS Gun Reporting
bills.summary: Requires the clerk of every judicial district court and the probate court to periodically report to the national instant criminal background check system the names of persons found incapacitated, committed to the state's alcohol and drug abuse program, or ordered into involuntary mental health treatment. Each report must describe the reason and note that it is made under the federal Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act. Clerks must cancel a record upon written request at least three years after the underlying guardianship is terminated, a commitment expires or is discharged, or a mental health case is sealed, subject to exceptions for repeat commitments. The act also clarifies that accessing medical records through the background check system does not constitute theft of medical records.

bills.title: BB Gun Not A Deadly Weapon
bills.summary: Revises the state's definition of a deadly weapon to clarify that a bee-bee gun or pellet gun is not one unless it is used to cause death or bodily injury. The definition otherwise covers any firearm, knife, bludgeon, or other weapon, device, or substance capable of producing death or serious bodily injury in the manner it is used or intended to be used. The act takes effect at the close of the ninety-day period after final adjournment that allows a referendum petition to be filed, or on the date of the official vote if a referendum is approved. Its provisions apply to offenses committed on or after that effective date.

bills.title: UnSafe Storage (Rapist Protection Act)
bills.summary: Creates a class 3 misdemeanor for a firearm owner or custodian who stores a firearm with criminal negligence and a person under eighteen then obtains it and unlawfully possesses it in a public place, uses it in violation of state or federal law, or discharges it. The offense does not apply if the young person obtains the firearm under direct parental or guardian supervision, in self-defense or defense of another, while defending a residence, or while attending a safety course, at a shooting range, or hunting under a valid license. It also exempts possession during organized competitions or performances, while traveling with an unloaded firearm to or from those activities, or as a result of a robbery or burglary. The penalty applies to offenses committed on or after July 1, 2002.

bills.title: Concealed Carry Restrictions
bills.summary: Creates a statewide concealed-handgun permit system in which county sheriffs must issue a permit to any legal resident age 21 or older who completes a certified handgun training class, passes a background check that includes fingerprinting sent to the bureau of investigation, and is not disqualified by a restraining order, chronic alcohol use, or controlled substance abuse.
