Sheriffs may deny a permit when documented behavior suggests the applicant would be a danger to self or others, and the denial is subject to judicial review. Permits are valid for five years and effective statewide except in areas where carrying is prohibited by federal law or on public school grounds. The act authorizes emergency permits for people in immediate danger, exempts certain peace officers, and recognizes reciprocal permits from other states.

bills.title: Concealed Weapons Permit Confidentiality
bills.summary: Requires any custodian of criminal justice records to keep confidential all identifying information about persons who hold concealed weapon permits, and defines all materials and records concerning those permits as exclusively criminal justice records outside the open records law. A custodian may exercise discretion in deciding whether to delete information identifying a person as a permit holder before releasing a record to an individual or agency. If the custodian chooses not to delete it, the person must receive written notice by registered mail or personal service, and the record cannot be released until ten days after the notice takes effect. Deletion is prohibited when the record goes to a criminal justice agency or when the permit holder is convicted of a crime involving the illegal use of a firearm.

bills.title: Insta-Check and Possession by Previous Offender
bills.summary: Modifies the crime of possession of a weapon by a previous offender so that a person adjudicated as a juvenile for an act that would be a felony may lawfully possess a firearm or other weapon if the act was a crime against property not used to coerce, control, or intimidate an intimate partner and the possession occurs at least ten years after the adjudication, release from commitment, or release from supervision. The act also limits the bureau of investigation's authority to deny a firearm transfer based on an arrest, charge, or filed indictment with no final disposition recorded in the databases to events within the seven years preceding the background check. The changes apply to both the underlying possession offense and the class 5 felony penalty that attaches when the weapon is a dangerous weapon. A safety clause declares the act necessary for the immediate preservation of public peace, health, and safety.

bills.title: Destruction of Government Records
bills.summary: Revises the definition of government records to expressly include computer software, programs, documentation, and data, while excluding library and museum materials, private papers, unsegregated electronic mail, and certain correspondence of elected officials. It creates a new class 6 felony for anyone who knowingly destroys, damages, or defaces any record of the state or a political subdivision, while leaving lawful records disposition performed under existing procedures untouched. The act also makes multi-year statutory appropriations to the corrections expansion reserve fund and the department of corrections. It takes effect on September 1, 2001, subject to the referendum petition period.

bills.title: CBI Background Registration System
bills.summary: Declares that completing the state's integrated criminal justice information system is critical to accurate and timely criminal background checks, and requires the criminal justice information program task force to establish uniform identifiers for matching records between the bureau of investigation and the judicial department's on-line court records network. Law enforcement, correctional, and judicial entities must forward arrest and fingerprint information to the bureau within seventy-two hours, and the bureau must electronically forward that information to the judicial department within twenty-four hours of receipt. The act also requires fingerprint-based criminal history checks for owners, employees, and residents of licensed child care facilities, with a comparison search of court records and a limited exemption for temporary out-of-state camp workers. Implementation is conditioned on a companion act producing net general fund savings equal to or greater than this act's appropriation.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry Uniform Statewide Criteria For Issuance
bills.summary: Creates a statewide concealed-handgun permit system administered by county sheriffs, requiring issuance to any legal resident age 21 or older who has no felony conviction or pending felony charges, no recent domestic violence misdemeanor, no outstanding arrest warrant, and no juvenile felony adjudication within the preceding ten years. Applicants must submit two sets of fingerprints, one of which the bureau of investigation sends to the federal bureau of investigation, and the bureau maintains a list of valid permit holders available only to law enforcement agencies. Permits are valid for five years and do not authorize carrying in areas prohibited by federal law, on government or school grounds, or in establishments that serve alcohol. The act exempts certain peace officers from the permit requirement, recognizes reciprocal permits from other states, and sets a uniform expiration date for permits issued before July 1, 2001.

bills.title: UnSafe Storage (Rapist Protection Act)
bills.summary: Creates a class 3 misdemeanor for a firearm owner or custodian who, through an act of criminal negligence, stores a firearm and a person under eighteen obtains it and then unlawfully possesses it in a public place, uses it in violation of state or federal law, or discharges it. The offense does not apply when the young person obtains the firearm under direct parental or guardian supervision, in lawful self-defense or defense of another, or while defending a residence against unlawful entry. It also exempts possession while attending a hunter or firearm safety course, at an authorized shooting range, while hunting under a valid license, or during organized competitions or performances, as well as travel with an unloaded firearm to or from those activities. The act takes effect at the close of the ninety-day referendum petition period following final adjournment and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Hunting Restrictions on Private Land
bills.summary: Adds a wildlife conservation hunting preference program under which a landowner holding at least one hundred sixty acres of agricultural land by recorded deed may apply for big game license applications for deer, elk, antelope, and other species, excluding moose and big horn sheep. Applications are allocated by acreage, from one for smaller parcels up to a maximum of six for holdings over six thousand acres, and are issued as a first priority within the fifteen percent limit on limited license units. Successful applicants receive transferable vouchers that eligible hunters may use to purchase licenses for the applicant's game management unit, and any unused preferences carry priority into the following year. The wildlife commission may also issue additional applications to landowners providing valuable habitat or public hunting access, and must adopt implementing rules before July 1, 2001.

bills.title: Concealed Carry Permit Holders Information Confidential
bills.summary: Requires the issuing law enforcement agency and any custodian of records to keep confidential the name, address, and telephone number of every person issued a concealed weapon permit, except that the information may be released to criminal justice agencies. All materials and records concerning concealed weapon permits are defined as exclusively criminal justice records, placing them outside the open records act. Any identifying information about a permit holder must be deleted from the record before it is released to an individual or agency other than a criminal justice agency. The deletion requirement does not apply when the permit holder is convicted of a crime involving the illegal use of a firearm.

bills.title: UnSafe Storage (Rapist Protection Act)
bills.summary: Makes it a class 3 misdemeanor for a person to negligently store a firearm in such a manner that a juvenile obtains possession of the firearm and uses it in violation of any provision of the state's criminal code or any municipal ordinance or county resolution. For purposes of the offense, negligently storing a firearm means placing or leaving it in a location where a reasonable person would perceive a substantial and unjustifiable risk that a juvenile would obtain possession of it. The act takes effect upon passage and applies only to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Prohibition of Firearms For Non-Violent Ex-Felons
bills.summary: Raises the penalty for the crime of possession of a weapon by a previous offender from class 1 misdemeanor to class 6 felony and requires any sentence for the offense to run consecutively with sentences the offender is already serving. The department of corrections must give every inmate a written advisement of the prohibited acts and penalties upon release, and any deferred judgment and sentence stipulation must contain the same advisement, which cannot be used as a defense or basis for appeal. A parole officer must file a complaint seeking revocation of parole for any parolee found in possession of a deadly weapon or arrested for a felony, a crime of violence, an assault involving a deadly weapon or bodily injury, or third degree sexual assault. The act also makes the offense ineligible for bail when the proof is evident, bars bail after conviction, and requires law enforcement to notify the corrections department within twenty-four hours when a parolee is arrested for it.

bills.title: Firearm Manufacturer Indemnification
bills.summary: Prohibits any person or public or private entity from bringing a tort action, other than a product liability action, against a firearms or ammunition manufacturer, importer, or dealer for injury, damage, or death caused by the discharge of a firearm or ammunition. It also bars holding such a maker liable as a third party for the actions of another person in any type of action, and requires courts to dismiss prohibited claims on a motion to dismiss while awarding the defendant reasonable attorney fees and costs. A tort action remains available for damages proximately caused by an act of the manufacturer, importer, or dealer that violates a state or federal statute or regulation, with the plaintiff bearing the burden of proving the violation by clear and convincing evidence. The act revises the state's legislative declaration to limit product liability for firearm discharge to actual defects in design or manufacture.

bills.title: Gun Purchase Restrictions
bills.summary: Makes it a class 4 felony for a person to knowingly purchase or otherwise obtain a firearm on behalf of, or for transfer to, someone the purchaser knows or reasonably should know is ineligible to possess a firearm under federal or state law. Licensed firearms dealers must post a sign displaying the prohibition in a manner easily readable by the public at each location where they sell firearms to the general public. A dealer who fails to post the sign commits a class 2 petty offense punishable by a fine of two hundred fifty dollars. The act also makes multi-year statutory appropriations to the corrections expansion reserve fund and the department of corrections, and applies to offenses committed on or after July 1, 2000.

bills.title: Under 21 Gun Show Purchase Prohibition
bills.summary: Prohibits the transfer of a handgun at a gun show to any person under 21 years of age and makes it unlawful for a person under 21 to purchase, trade, or rent a handgun at a gun show. The bill defines a gun show as an event sponsored by an organization devoted to the collection, competitive use, or other sporting use of firearms, and includes transactions occurring in any parking area used for the event. It requires a transferor to request identification from any transferee before transferring a handgun and makes a violation a class 1 misdemeanor, while a knowing transfer of a handgun to a person under 21 is a class 4 felony. The bill also criminalizes knowingly making a false statement or presenting misrepresented identification intended to deceive a transferor about a material fact, and makes a 5-year statutory appropriation.
sponsors: Rep. Zimmerman, Sen. Phillips, Sen. Weddig

bills.title: Required Background Checks At Gun Shows
bills.summary: Requires a transferor of a firearm at a gun show to contact the Colorado bureau of investigation and request a criminal background check on the prospective transferee before the transfer. The bureau must conduct a state and, to the extent allowed by federal law, a federal criminal background check, and then either issue a transaction number authorizing the transfer or deny authorization if the transferee is ineligible to possess a firearm or is the subject of an unresolved charge or indictment. A transfer at a gun show without first obtaining a transaction number is a class 1 misdemeanor, as is knowingly transferring a firearm to a person prohibited from possessing one, and a knowing transfer of a handgun to a juvenile is a class 4 felony. The prospective transferee bears the cost of the check, the bureau must destroy the background check records within 48 hours while retaining the transaction number and any denial records, and the act takes effect 90 days after final adjournment or, if a referendum petition is filed, on the date of the official vote declaration.

bills.title: Prohibited Gun Sales To Persons Under 21
bills.summary: Makes it unlawful for a federally licensed importer, manufacturer, dealer, or collector to sell or deliver any firearm or ammunition, other than a shotgun or rifle or ammunition for a shotgun or rifle, to an individual the licensee knows or should reasonably know is under 21 years of age. A licensee who sells or delivers a firearm in violation of that prohibition commits the offense of unlawful sale of a firearm to a person under 21, which is a class 4 felony. The bill defines firearm, licensed collector, licensed dealer, licensed importer, licensed manufacturer, rifle, and shotgun to carry the same meanings as in the federal Gun Control Act of 1968. It takes effect upon passage and applies to offenses committed on or after that date, and makes a 5-year statutory appropriation.

bills.title: Prohibit Local Governments From Regulating Firearms/Preemption
bills.summary: Declares firearms regulation a matter of statewide concern and prohibits any municipality, county, or city and county from enacting an ordinance or resolution that restricts a person's ability to own, possess, carry, repair, manufacture, display, or transfer a firearm to a greater extent than state statute. The bill does not limit a local government's authority to regulate the areas or circumstances under which a person may discharge a firearm. An ordinance or resolution that imposes a greater penalty than a comparable state statute is treated as a greater restriction, and any such local measure in existence on the effective date that violates the act is deemed unauthorized and unenforceable for events on or after that date. The bill also amends the concealed weapons permit statute to bar a sheriff or chief of police from requiring an applicant to disclose the brand, model, caliber, or serial number of any firearm the applicant owns or uses.

bills.title: Firearms Prohibition At The State Capitol
bills.summary: Adds a joint rule of the senate and house prohibiting any person, including members of the general assembly, from bringing or possessing a firearm or explosive or incendiary device on the property of, or within any building used by, the legislature unless the person first obtains written authorization. Authorization must come from the speaker for house areas, the senate president for senate areas, or both for joint areas, and the request must describe the device, the date and place, and the purpose. A state patrol officer must inspect the device on entry, keep any firearm unloaded with the bolt open and safety engaged, and accompany the person at all times while the device is on legislative property. The rule does not apply to holders of a written concealed weapon permit or to certain peace officers and federal probation officers while on duty.

bills.title: Firearm Manufacturer Indemnification (Senate Version)
bills.summary: Prohibits a civil action in tort, other than a product liability action, against a firearms or ammunition manufacturer or dealer or against any firearms trade association for damages arising from physical or emotional injury, physical damage, or death caused by the discharge of a firearm or ammunition, including any action alleging the defendant is liable as a third party for the actions of another person. Upon a motion to dismiss, the court must dismiss a prohibited action and award reasonable attorney fees, in addition to costs, to each named defendant. The bill also revises the legislative declaration to state that product liability for injury, damage, or death caused by a firearm or ammunition is based only on an actual defect in its design or manufacture, not on the inherent potential of a firearm to cause harm when discharged or on any theory holding the manufacturer liable for another person's actions. The act takes effect upon passage and applies to causes of action arising on or after that date.

bills.title: Mandatory Background Check For Firearm Transfers
bills.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor for a person to knowingly transfer a firearm to anyone prohibited from possessing a firearm under state or federal law. It also makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to transfer a firearm without first receiving a transaction number from the Colorado bureau of investigation, and requires a transferor to contact the bureau to request a criminal background check on the prospective transferee. The bureau must perform a state and, if possible, a federal criminal background check and then either provide a transaction number or deny authorization for the transfer based on whether the check shows the transferee is ineligible to possess a firearm. The prospective transferee bears the cost of the check, the bureau must purge the records created in conducting the check while retaining a list of the transaction numbers issued, and the bill makes it a class 1 misdemeanor to make a false statement or present misrepresented identification when attempting to acquire a firearm.

bills.title: CBI Firearms Background Check System
bills.summary: Designates the Colorado bureau of investigation as the state point of contact for implementing the national instant criminal background check system created by the federal Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act. While serving in that role, the bureau must meet or exceed federal standards and may, by law or rule, pursue its own policy so long as it is consistent with federal law. The bill amends the bureau's functions to carry out the statewide duties of the national instant criminal background check system in connection with the transfer of firearms, and defines a transfer to include the sale or delivery of any firearm in the state and the redemption of a pawned firearm by a person who is not a federal firearms licensee, while excluding the return or replacement of a firearm delivered to a federal licensee solely for repair or customizing. It makes a statutory appropriation to implement the measure.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Carry Uniform Statewide Criteria For Issuance
bills.summary: Declares the issuance of concealed handgun permits a matter of statewide concern and requires any police chief or sheriff who chooses to issue such permits to establish a concealed handgun permit program within the jurisdiction. To the extent fiscally practicable, the police chiefs and sheriffs must adopt standardized applications and standardized permits. A police chief or sheriff may issue a permit to any applicant who is at least 21 years old, is a Colorado resident, and meets specified firearms training requirements, provided the applicant can legally possess a firearm under federal law and has not been convicted of or adjudicated for a felony or certain misdemeanors and is not subject to unresolved criminal proceedings, chronically or habitually using alcohol or controlled substances, a danger due to mental problems, or otherwise a danger to self or others. A concealed handgun permit issued by this state, or by another state under a comparable statute, is valid in all areas of the state, and a permittee must carry the permit and a valid photo ID when carrying a concealed handgun.

bills.title: Background Checks At Gun Shows
bills.summary: Submits to registered electors a proposed amendment to article XVIII of the constitution requiring a background check on a prospective firearm transferee whenever any part of the transaction occurs at a gun show. The measure directs a gun show vendor to require a background check on a prospective transferee and to obtain approval of the transfer from the Colorado bureau of investigation, and requires gun show promoters to arrange for the services of federally licensed gun dealers to obtain those background checks. It prohibits the transfer of a firearm if a background check has not been obtained by a federally licensed gun dealer, requires record keeping and retention by the dealers who obtain the checks, and permits them to charge a fee of up to ten dollars per check. The measure also requires promoters to prominently post notice of the background check requirement, establishes criminal penalties for violations, exempts transfers of certain antique firearms, relics, and curios, and requires the appropriation of funds to implement it, taking effect if a majority of electors vote in favor.

bills.title: Standardization Of Firearms Regs
bills.summary: Recognizes that firearms regulation is a matter of statewide concern and prohibits any municipality, county, or city and county from adopting an ordinance or resolution that would impose a greater restriction on a person's ability to own, possess, carry, use, or transfer a firearm than is imposed by state law. The bill identifies the imposition of a greater penalty as a greater restriction and specifies that any ordinance or resolution in existence on the effective date that violates the act is deemed unauthorized and unenforceable on or after that date. It also changes the affirmative defenses to the charge of carrying concealed weapons into exceptions.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Permits
bills.summary: Declares the issuance of permits to carry concealed handguns a matter of statewide concern and instructs each sheriff to implement and administer the permit provisions, while providing that the state occupies the field of regulation of bearing concealed handguns for self-defense and that sheriffs do not have authority to regulate or restrict the issuing of permits beyond what the bill provides. The bill specifies the qualifications for receiving a permit, including age, state residency, ability to possess a firearm under state and federal law, whether the applicant uses alcoholic beverages illegally or excessively, and competence with a handgun. It specifies the contents of the permit and how the permit may be used and identifies conditions under which a handgun is not considered concealed. An applicant must submit an application and a permit fee to a sheriff, who is instructed to witness the applicant's signature on the application.

bills.title: Prohibition Of Firearms Straw Purchasers
bills.summary: Makes it a class 1 misdemeanor for a person to knowingly purchase or otherwise obtain a firearm on behalf of, or for transfer to, a person who is ineligible to possess a firearm under federal or state law or ineligible to purchase a firearm in this state. The bill requires a licensed firearm dealer, as defined in federal law, to post a sign displaying that prohibition in a manner that is easily readable and visible to the public at each location where the dealer sells firearms to the general public. It takes effect July 1, 1999, and applies to offenses committed on or after that date.

bills.title: Juvenile Access To Handguns
bills.summary: Prohibits unsafe storage of a loaded handgun by any person in control of premises who knows or reasonably should know that a juvenile under 16 is likely to gain access to it. The bill requires such a person to keep the handgun in a securely locked box, container, cabinet, or store room, in a location a reasonable person would believe to be secure, or to secure it with a trigger lock. A person who violates the requirement commits a class 5 felony if a juvenile obtains the handgun and uses it to inflict injury or death upon any person, and commits a class 3 misdemeanor if a juvenile accesses it without adult supervision and possesses or exhibits it in a public place or in a careless, angry, or threatening manner. The felony does not apply if the juvenile obtained the handgun through an unlawful entry, from armed forces, National Guard, state militia, or law enforcement personnel during official duties, or if the person in control was carrying it on the body or in close proximity, and the bill provides for additional exceptions.

bills.title: Implement Federal Firearm Instant Check
bills.summary: Authorizes the Colorado bureau of investigation to act as the state point of contact for implementing the permanent provisions of the federal Brady law and authorizes the bureau's director to promulgate the rules necessary for the bureau to carry out those duties. The bill adds to the grounds for denial of a firearm transfer under state law the grounds of being the subject of an information or felony complaint or having been arrested or charged with a crime that, if convicted, would prohibit the arrestee from receiving a firearm. It requires the bureau to provide notice of a denial to the law enforcement agencies having jurisdiction over the area where the transferee resides and where the transferor conducts business. The director may charge a fee to cover the direct and indirect costs incurred in processing instant criminal background checks, and the bill creates a cash fund for those fees.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Permits
bills.summary: Requires the public safety director of each city and county and each sheriff to establish a concealed handgun permit program for issuing permits within their jurisdictions. The bill requires each public safety director and sheriff to issue a concealed handgun permit to anyone who is at least 25 years old, is a Colorado resident, and meets specified firearms training requirements, so long as the applicant has not been convicted of or adjudicated for a felony or certain misdemeanors and is not subject to unresolved criminal proceedings, chronically or habitually using alcohol or controlled substances, a danger due to mental problems, or otherwise a danger to self or others. It requires the public safety director or sheriff to conduct a criminal background check, including a fingerprint check, and to deny a permit if the applicant does not qualify as provided in the act. The bill also identifies procedures for appealing a denial of a permit.

bills.title: Restrictions On Local Firearm Ordinances
bills.summary: Prohibits local governments from regulating firearms, reserving that authority to the state.

bills.title: Concealed Handgun Permits
bills.summary: Specifies that the issuance of permits to carry concealed handguns is a matter of statewide concern and assigns responsibility for issuing the permits to county sheriffs and the official having the duties of a sheriff in any city and county. The bill specifies the qualifications for receiving a permit, including residency, age, criminal history, whether the applicant is the subject of a restraining order or an emergency protection order, illegal or excessive use of controlled substances or alcoholic beverages, mental health, competence with a handgun, and whether the sheriff has grounds to believe the applicant would be dangerous to self or others. It specifies the contents of the permit and how the permit may be used and identifies conditions under which a handgun is not considered concealed. An applicant must submit an application, a permit fee, and, in some circumstances, a photograph to a sheriff, who is instructed to verify identity, take two full sets of fingerprints, and determine whether the applicant qualifies, with procedures for denying a permit including judicial review.
